labels.label: T-abs-hoist-time-function/has-time-function
findings: Library, not paper: the docstring of Causality.HasTimeFunction in Causal/CBG/Pgcd.lean (HEAD :123-132) said it 'is weaker than the strict library's Causality.IsTimeFunction ... and than IsCauchyTimeFunction'. That is false. The notions are incomparable. An ETT time function (a strong morphism to timelikeLine) is only non-decreasing: the doubled line has one with no strictly increasing continuous function, since it is not causal (exists_isTimeFunction_not_isCausal, kb/0058). Conversely, HasTimeFunction asks neither openness nor ≤_U/≪_U preservation on every open. The moved docstring (Causal/CurvesExtend.lean:505-515) now says 'neither ... nor', and the def's code is unchanged.
questions: Reading taken: the definition goes at the top level of namespace Causal in Causal.CurvesExtend (:516), after the section on Cauchy surfaces and under a new header '### The ladder node time_function', with its two code lines verbatim. Its own binders {M : Type*} [TopologicalSpace M] (C : Causality M) shadow the section variable M, which is therefore not included. Type, universe list [u_1], binder telescope and value hash are identical (dump). Pgcd also gains an explicit `import Causal.CurvesExtend`. That import is redundant, since Pgcd reaches it through Injective, but the dispatch asks that Pgcd import it.

labels.new: Causal/CurvesExtend.lean:526 `theorem Causality.HasTimeFunction.curvesExtend {C : Causality M} (h : C.HasTimeFunction) : C.CurvesExtend` (obtain, then curvesExtend_of_timeFunction). :536 `theorem Causality.HasTimeFunction.isCausal {C : Causality M} (h : C.HasTimeFunction) : C.IsCausal` (obtain; x ≤ y ≤ x, x ≠ y gives T x < T y < T x). Both have docstrings, use the standard three axioms only and live in the ETT layer. A first version of curvesExtend written with a term-mode `let ⟨_, hTc, hT⟩ := h` created an auxiliary matcher `HasTimeFunction.curvesExtend.match_1_1`. It was rewritten in tactic mode, so these two are the only new public constants. Ladder probe, in /tmp only, with neither ladder.toml nor Rules.lean touched: the dry-run `emit-lean` output combined with Test emits time_function ⇒ curves_extend now that CurvesExtend is ETT-layer, and adds two Test examples `(_h0 : HasTimeFunction C) : CurvesExtend C / IsCausal C := by causal_ladder`. With the current witnesses (curvesExtend_of_timeFunction, isCausal_of_exists_timeFunction) both examples FAIL (aesop does not unfold HasTimeFunction). With the witnesses switched to these two wrappers the whole generated Rules+Test compiles, including the no-model guard and the 32 new `fail_if_success` checks.
